title: Technological change and development

blocks.heading: Technological change and development
blocks.text: Micro-electronics, biotechnology and communication and information systems can change how production is organised and how people access knowledge and markets. Their development benefits depend on access, relevant skills and supporting infrastructure; unequal access can widen existing opportunity gaps. Digital ordering may connect a producer to buyers, but a connection alone does not supply transport or material inputs. Technological change can alter who coordinates production and which tasks workers perform. Explain these mechanisms rather than assuming a new device improves everyone’s life.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Micro-electronics
blocks.text: Micro-electronics uses very small electronic components and integrated circuits in devices and control systems. Electronic monitoring and control can improve the timing or precision of production where equipment, operators and maintenance are suitable. A sensor and controller can regulate the temperature of a productive process, reducing avoidable variation. The device still needs appropriate setup and reliable power. A claim about improved quality must follow from what the control actually changes, not from the word electronic.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Biotechnology
blocks.text: Biotechnology uses living organisms, cells or biological processes to make or improve products or processes. Fermentation and controlled biological production illustrate biotechnology; an ordinary electronic machine does not qualify merely because it is modern. Using yeast to make dough rise is a biological process. A digital sales register records information without itself applying organisms or biological processes. Biotechnology is broader than genetic modification, which is one possible application. Classify the mechanism, not the age or sophistication of the equipment.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Communications and information systems
blocks.text: Communication systems transmit information, while information systems collect, process, store or organise it for use. Timely and usable information can improve coordination, but access, skills, connectivity and the ability to act on it affect the benefit. An invented producer receiving confirmed orders electronically can plan quantities and arrange delivery sooner. If a road remains closed, better information does not move the goods. Information may reduce one uncertainty while leaving a different constraint intact.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect information to an actual opportunity
blocks.text: An invented producer receives electronic orders a day earlier than before. It has stock, a vehicle and an open route, so earlier information can help combine deliveries and avoid late dispatch. If the route closes, the same message will not remove the transport constraint. In a separate example, yeast fermentation in dough is biotechnology because a biological process creates the change. A touchscreen payment device is micro-electronic or information technology rather than biotechnology merely because it is modern.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Concrete information and biological applications
blocks.text: Micro-electronic sensors can monitor processing temperatures, while programmable controls adjust operations. Communication systems can coordinate buyer orders and delivery times; stock records can warn when inputs need replacing. Biotechnology uses organisms or biological processes for a useful purpose, including developing and propagating crop varieties suited to growing conditions. Such changes can automate repetitive tasks and create demand for new operating or repair skills; they need suitable training rather than guaranteeing more employment.
